thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED - prod write errors after recent rollout. Service=web-api, deploy=release/2026-03-15-12. Canary passed but promotion at 12:03. Paging on-call @alex. Incident ID INC-20260315-42

alex: On it. Getting into the cluster now. Any idea what changed in this release?

maria: We shipped a schema migration + app change: migration 20260315_add_activity_flags. Migration does: 
```sql
ALTER TABLE activity ADD COLUMN flags jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' ;
```
Canary showed a few transient timeouts (~1-2%) but we promoted at 12:03.

samir: Confirming - the ALTER with default triggered a table rewrite on the activity table and got an AccessExclusive lock. Saw a backlog of waiting backends. This is causing 500s for write endpoints.

zoe: Observability: 12:05-12:12 UTC spike in 500s for /events ingest and /activity.create. Error rate peaked at 28% in us-east-1. Latency for writes also spiked.

alex: Rolling back the app deploy now to limit surface. @deploy-bot kick it off.

deploy-bot: rolling back web-api from release/2026-03-15 to release/2026-03-14 (v2.11.1). Start time 12:09 UTC. Health checks will be monitored.

maria: FYI rollback won't unblock the DB locks if the migration process is still running on the DB primary. The ALTER was started from the migration job on the new release.

samir: I'm seeing the active migration backend:
```sql
SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS runtime, query 
FROM pg_stat_activity 
WHERE query ILIKE '%ALTER TABLE activity%' AND state = 'active';
 pid | runtime  | query
-----+----------+-------------------------------------------
 4523 | 00:00:48 | ALTER TABLE activity ADD COLUMN flags ...
```
It's holding an AccessExclusive lock; waiting backends piled up.

alex: Can we cancel that backend? What's safe?

samir: Two options: pg_cancel_backend(pid) to ask it to stop cleanly; if it ignores, pg_terminate_backend(pid) to force kill. Cancel first. After cancel we should avoid re-running the aggressive ALTER with default; instead add nullable column then backfill.

alex: Running cancel now.

samir: result: cancel didn't stop the process, it's still stuck in processing (the table rewrite is in kernel). We'll need to terminate. I'll pg_terminate_backend(4523) in 30s unless objections.

infra-bot: (audit) runbook note - terminating backends can roll back the transaction in-flight. Expect partial progress on ALTER.

leah: Customer-facing: Support queue shows multiple customers reporting 502/500s for streaming ingestion. I'll start an incident status update to affected customers.

samir: Terminated PID 4523. Locks cleared. Verified via:
```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE relation = 'activity'::regclass AND locktype = 'relation';
-- returns 0
```
Writes are accepting again.

zoe: Error rate dropped back to baseline within 90s of termination. Rolling window shows 3% errors now, down from 28%.

alex: Good. I also toggled the feature flag for the new ingest path to off to reduce risk while we fix the DB migration: 
```bash
ff-cli toggle events_ingest_v2 --off --env=prod --actor=alex
```
Command returned: feature events_ingest_v2 set to OFF (propagated to all regions).

maria: Next steps for safe schema change:
1) ALTER TABLE activity ADD COLUMN flags jsonb; -- no default, nullable (fast)
2) Backfill flags in batches (background job)
3) Once backfill complete, ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN flags SET NOT NULL; then set default if needed

samir: I'll run the first step now (nullable add). Doing: 
```sql
ALTER TABLE activity ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS flags jsonb;
```
This is fast and takes milliseconds (no table rewrite).

samir: Backfill strategy: python scripts/backfill_activity_flags.py --batch-size=2000 --limit 1000000
This will run in controlled batches and update a small percentage at a time to avoid I/O spikes.

alex: While backfill runs, we should keep the feature flag off and keep the old binary in prod. We'll only roll forward when >=99% backfill complete and no regressions.

leah: Customer comms draft: "We're investigating write errors after a schema migration and have mitigated production impact. We've rolled back the recent app release, terminated an in-progress migration that caused locks, and applied a safer migration path. We'll follow up with timeline for full restore." Sending to legal & account execs.

peter: Incident commander update: Impact reduced, mitigation in place. Suspected root cause: migration with default triggered table rewrite and locks. Moving to short-term mitigation -> backfill plan -> scheduled safe promote. Assigning owners: samir (db migration), maria (release lead), alex (oncall / rollout decision).

samir: Kicking the backfill now in batches. I'll post progress updates every 15m. Current ETA: ~3 hours for full dataset at configured batch size.

zoe: Monitoring: write error rate trending down. Canary will be re-enabled at 10% traffic after we hit 50% backfilled and hold for 15m.

alex: On-call handoff note: I'm handing to morning shift @maria in 2.5 hours. Maria, please monitor backfill and hold any promotion until you confirm backfill completion and no regressions.

maria: Acknowledged - I'll take over the incident and coordinate the safe rollout once samir gives the green light.

peter: Moving to status: mitigated -> monitoring. Will open a postmortem ticket and set follow-ups: (1) migration-runbook update to avoid ALTER ... DEFAULT table rewrites, (2) add pre-deploy DB change checklist, (3) improve deploy gating on long-running DDLs.

leah: I'll send the customer update now and add affected accounts list.

alex: Thanks team. Leaving the channel but reachable if needed.

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder - incident on-call transferring from alex -> maria at 15:00 UTC.

peter: Closing active pager; incident remains in monitoring. Postmortem owner: maria.
